00:00 Speaker 1 (Ethan): okay everybody thanks for joining, i'm Ethan from Redwood Inference, i'll run the agenda quick, priya's gonna cover the runtime and pilot config, marta will handle onboarding cadence.
02:03 Speaker 2 (Samir): yeah thanks, we — hi all — we wanted to make sure this pilot proves cost and latency improvements compared to our current self-hosted flow, and also that we can keep everything in our VPC.
04:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): totally, for context the pilot we're proposing is a small dedicated pool, 2-4 gpus, short sequence lengths, we can instrument p95 latency and token cost. quick Q: are you planning on KV cache reuse across requests?
06:08 Speaker 4 (Janae): um we do a mix, some of our endpoints use prefix caching, some are stateless. we can provide traces. one thing: our security team insists on customer-managed KMS for key wrapping, is that supported?
08:12 Speaker 2 (Samir): and we need SOC2 artifacts and audit logging for the pilot, even initial access.
10:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes on KMS we have integrations for customer KMS/HSM in Private mode, it's a config we wire during onboarding, for Hosted we'd offer a managed KMS but for Private you'll keep control. audit logs appear in the console and we can forward to your SIEM.
12:18 Speaker 5 (Victor): slight interrup — sorry, how does the KV cache persist across dedicated nodes? do you replicate or is there sticky routing?
14:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): good point, we do a combination: for Dedicated we can enable sticky routing per customer session or use a distributed prefix cache. for the pilot with 2 nodes we recommend sticky to keep tail latency predictable. that reduces cross-node fetches.
16:23 Speaker 1 (Ethan): on the commercial side, we'll price the pilot as a time-boxed dedicated commit with a modest uplift and a usage overage bucket, we'll send a draft.
18:26 Speaker 4 (Janae): what's the fallback if a node fails during the test? do you have automatic graceful degrade to smaller models?
20:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): yep we have smart routing with model variants; if the primary model hits capacity or a node drops, requests can route to a compatible quantized variant or a hosted fallback depending on policy you pick. we can demo that in the stress run.
22:31 Speaker 2 (Samir): perfect. success metrics: p95 latency < 180ms for single-turn prompts, 99.9% availability for the window, and cost per 1k tokens under our current baseline by 20%. are those realistic?
24:33 Speaker 3 (Priya): p95 under 180 is doable with sticky routing and warm kv cache for short sequences, though it depends on your tokenization and model size. we'll run a baseline test to calibrate.
26:36 Speaker 5 (Victor): on compliance: we also need SAML SSO for console access and RBAC scoped to team roles, also IP allowlist and VPC peering.
28:39 Speaker 3 (Priya): SAML and RBAC are supported, we map SAML groups to roles; IP allowlist + VPC peering and private control plane are in Private deployment. we'll attach our SAML mapping guide.
30:41 Speaker 6 (Riley): curious about observability — what telemetry do we get out of the box? token-level cost? per-route latency?
32:43 Speaker 3 (Priya): Console gives per-route token breakdowns, p95/p50 latency, error traces, and request sampling for debugging. we can add custom tracing hooks and send logs to your datadog/splunk.
34:45 Speaker 1 (Ethan): competitor note: we heard you were evaluating anthropic's managed endpoints, right? where's the tie-breaker?
36:47 Speaker 2 (Samir): yeah anthro — our infra team liked the simplicity, but the ability to run private and to tweak batching and quantization with operator controls is the big sell for us. also better unit economics.
38:49 Speaker 3 (Priya): for batching we can provide presets; i saw in your questionnaire you have many short requests so aggressive batching might hurt latency, we usually recommend micro-batching + prefix cache for that pattern.
40:51 Speaker 4 (Janae): what's required from our infra to allow the benchmark window? ephemeral peering? firewall rules?
42:53 Speaker 3 (Priya): we'll need an allowlist of Redwood egress IPs, a temporary peering or VPN tunnel for Private control plane, and access to your sample payloads. we have a short doc with exact CIDR ranges.
44:55 Speaker 1 (Ethan): ok, let's recap next steps — priya will share runbook, i'll send pricing, victor you'll send security contacts, janae will confirm networking window.
46:57 Speaker 2 (Samir): sounds good. any blockers on the timeline? we want to start benchmarking next week so please send docs asap.
47:45 Speaker 3 (Priya): we'll aim to share artifacts by end of day tomorrow, and propose Tue/Wed benchmark windows. thanks everyone.
